rationale: analyze_expression: no derivatives, no integrals, no ungoverned functions, explicitly_solvable_for_target=true - a static explicit relation for the axial magnetic flux density of a thick, elastically-compliant circular loop with steady curvature-induced current crowding. B_z is the output; I, a, z, radial_observation_coordinate are the sampled inputs (the pipeline's 'time axis' label is a category tag, not real time). vacuum_permeability, wire_cross_section_radius, dc_current_crowding_factor, loop_radial_compliance are fixed physical constants; vacuum_permeability MUST be 4*pi*1e-7 T*m/A - auto_balance's suggestion to rescale it to 1e6 was rejected. Ranges keep the observation point strictly inside the loop annulus (r<=0.03 m, a>=0.06 m gives |a-r|>=0.03 m, so the (a-r)^2+z^2 denominators never approach zero), keep the Gauss-Chebyshev-like sum well-conditioned, let the (rw/a) power series converge (rw/a<=0.033, rw^8/a^8 ~ 1e-12), and keep log(8a/rw)=ln(240..600) moderate. Currents up to 100 A push the NEW loop_radial_compliance*mu0*I^2/2*(ln(8a/rw)-1) term above 5*sigma (multiple 6.65) while the implied radius perturbation stays ~3e-5 m << 0.05*a. Noise sigma=1e-9 T is ~1e-6 of the on-axis center field, at the fluxgate/SQUID measurement floor. excitation_ok=false because a handful of asymptotic r^10/r^12 * rw^{2..8} Taylor-tail terms have absolute amplitudes 1e-16 to 1e-13 T - orders of magnitude below any measurement floor and physically negligible for the phenomenon; no physical parameter choice or physical range makes them visible without violating the compliance-linearity or wire-thin-loop assumptions the label imposes. Since this is explicit, evaluate_explicit is the integrator and no initial conditions or state_variables are needed.
